calls.head: The matchup inside the matchup
calls.body: The Penguins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, and the Flyers are one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Penguins’ chance quality wins out.
calls.call: The Penguins’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Flyers.
calls.nums: Pittsburgh 5th for chance quality (a 6.6% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Philadelphia 5th for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On chance quality, Pittsburgh had 7.2% a shot. The league average is 6.3% a shot, and they came in at 6.6% a shot.

calls.head: Something has to give
calls.body: The Flyers are near the top of the league for the power play, and the Penguins are near the top of the league at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Penguins’ kill holds up, even though power plays usually win these.
calls.call: The Penguins’ kill holds the Flyers’ power play under the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: Philadelphia 7th for the power play (7.8 expected goals per 60) · Pittsburgh 6th for the penalty kill

calls.happened: On the power play, Philadelphia had 6.6 per 60. The league average is 7.6 per 60, and they came in at 7.8 per 60.

calls.head: Bruisers against finesse
calls.body: The Flyers are near the top of the league for physicality, at the bruising end; the Penguins are one of the league’s worst, at the finesse end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Flyers hit more than the Penguins in the close stretches of the game.

PHI.head: We had this close to even (58% for Philadelphia), and it went Pittsburgh’s way.

PIT.head: We had this close to even (42% for Pittsburgh), and Pittsburgh came through.

surprises.head: Philadelphia couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Philadelphia’s shots at 5-on-5 were less dangerous than usual: a 3.7% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.6% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 250 games.

surprises.head: Pittsburgh tried a different line
surprises.body: N. Robertson, R. Rakell, S. Crosby played 10:08 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Pittsburgh’s usual lines.

story.head: Silovs shuts out the Flyers
paras: Nick Robertson scored twice, opening the scoring midway through the first. Six different Penguins scored. Arturs Silovs stopped all 19 shots.

The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Penguins win nine in ten. By our Swing measure, Filip Hallander had the best night of anyone. The Penguins tried a line they hadn’t used before: Robertson, Rickard Rakell and Sidney Crosby, and it had a hand in three of their goals.

items.text: Whether the Penguins keep that line together at home against Montréal on Saturday.
Two of the preview’s three calls held.
